High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Shri S.K. Kashyap - Government Advocate for the respond
Shri D.K. Shukla - Advocate for the objector.

Heard on I.A No.9554/2023 an application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant - Vivek Kumar Sharma arising out of judgment dated 10.11.2022 delivered in Sessions Case No.05/2021 by the Special Judge, POCSO Act, 2012,
Singrauli, Head Quarter Waidhan, District Singrauli.
The appellant has been convicted under Section 376(2)(i) of the I.P.C. and sentenced to undergo R.I.
for 15 years with fine of Rs.30,000/-, with default stipulation.

As per prosecution story, the prosecutrix lodged a report in Police Station Waidhan on 20.10.2020 that when she visited her sister's house in village Dighi in the year 2017, brother of her "Jija" namely present appellant sexually assaulted her.
Thereafter, on 16.05.2017 in village Telai, the appellant again allegedly committed rape.
Thereafter, on 28.06.2017 in Kachani Mandir, the appellant allegedly sexually assaulted her.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that determination of age by the Court below is erroneous.

The Admission Register was produced by Mahendra Kumar Pandey (PW/5), but he could not produce the declaration form filled up by the parents, which is the statutory requirement as per the rules of M.P. Date of Birth (Entries in the School Register) Rules,
1973.
The mother of prosecutrix (PW/2) deposed that she cannot narrate the age/date of birth of victim with accuracy and precision.
The victim was admitted in the school by her uncle Deepak Sharma, who is no more.
For 3 years the family of victim waited for appellant and when he did not turn up, the FIR was lodged.
The same is the stand of victim's father (PW/3).
Since age is not properly determined, the provisions of POCSO Act are not attracted.
The inordinate and unexplained delay in FIR causes serious doubt on the story of prosecution.
The final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future.
Thus, remaining jail sentence of this appellant may be suspended.

sentences.text: Learned Government Advocate for the State and learned counsel for the objector opposed the prayer on the basis of objection.

Considering the enormous and unexplained delay in lodging the FIR coupled with aforesaid factual backdrop, without expressing any opinion on merits, we deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of appellant.
Accordingly, I.A. No.9554/2023 is allowed.

Subject to depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited), the remaining jail sentence of appellant - Vivek Kumar Sharma is hereby suspended and it is directed that appellant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the trial Court, Waidhan, District Singrauli on 9th of October, 2023 and also on such other dates as may be fixed by the said Court in this regard during the pendency of this Appeal.
Certified copy as per rules.
